dailyInsight.headline: Test whether compaction can still call a tool it has forgotten
dailyInsight.insight: Pydantic AI now treats deferred-tool availability as evidence in the surviving conversation, not as a permanent memory of a prior discovery. Builders who compact, replay, or resume Pydantic AI agent histories should test one deferred-tool path: after the reveal or capability load falls behind a compaction boundary, a direct call should be refused until the agent searches or loads again.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The reported change filters revealed names whose deferred capability is not represented as loaded in the current history, withholds those tools from the model's callable set, and returns a retry that identifies the recovery step. A capability loaded during one response becomes usable on the next request, when its instructions and tools can actually reach the model.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Context compaction and deferred tools both save prompt space, but they can otherwise leave a runtime willing to execute a name the current model context no longer explains. A bounded replay test can expose that mismatch before a resumed agent acts on an old tool assumption.

actions.audience: Builder or operator of a Pydantic AI agent that uses deferred tools or capabilities and can compact, replay, or resume history
actions.label: Exercise one compacted deferred-tool path
actions.instruction: In a disposable run with a harmless test tool, reveal or load one deferred capability, compact or replay the history, then request the old tool name. Verify that the call is refused without execution, that the recovery message directs the agent to search or load again, and that a later request after that recovery can call the tool. Do not use production credentials or destructive tools.

receipts.title: Require a deferred tool to be revealed, and its capability loaded, before it can be called (#7271)
receipts.supports: Shows the new availability gate, history-derived capability state, callable-set filtering, documentation edits, and focused regression tests for unavailable tool calls.

receipts.title: Compaction capability documentation at commit da29bfa
receipts.supports: States that a tool whose reveal evidence is behind a compaction boundary is refused until the agent searches for or loads it again.

confidence.basis: A fresh public implementation change, its accompanying documentation, and the focused availability tests agree on a narrow Pydantic AI runtime contract. The recommendation is a reversible test of that contract, not a claim about deployment or every agent framework.

dailyInsight.limitation: These main-branch source receipts do not establish a released package, production behavior, history integrity, or compatibility across providers and other agent runtimes. The availability rule is not a substitute for an authorization system or trusted server-side history.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public integration tests show a compacted or replayed Pydantic AI history can execute an unavailable deferred tool without a fresh reveal or capability load, or if an officially documented runtime path intentionally keeps such a tool callable after its evidence is removed.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for release notes and integration tests covering compacted, replayed, provider-switched, and client-submitted histories, especially whether the retry guidance remains actionable without creating a loop.
